text: 素人じゃないよな どこの地位は?
translation: You're no amateur, are you. Which team are you from?

vocabulary.meaning: isn't it, are you not (negative form used rhetorically)
team (note: 地位 normally means 'rank/status'; spoken usage here likely means チーム)

grammar: じゃないよな is a rhetorical negative seeking confirmation — 'you're not an amateur, right?' The second sentence どこの地位は? is elliptical, dropping the verb; context (blitzball practice) makes 'which team are you from?' clear.

text: どっから来たって? / あ、悪い
translation: Where did you say you came from? / Oh, my bad.

vocabulary.meaning: from where (colloquial contraction of どこから)
quotation/question particle; 'you said…?' or 'did you say…?'

grammar: どっから来たって is a casual reported-question — Wakka is asking what Tidus just said. 悪い as a standalone is an informal apology, short for 悪かった or 悪いな.

text: 今のなし
translation: Forget what I just said.

vocabulary.meaning: the just-now one, what I just said

grammar: 今のなし is an idiomatic colloquial phrase meaning 'that doesn't count' or 'ignore what I just said.' It works as a complete utterance with no verb needed.

text: 俺さ、シンに近づきすぎて / 頭がぐるぐるなんだよな / だから、どこから来たとか
translation: Me, I got too close to Sin, so my head's all spinning — that's why, things like where I'm from…

vocabulary.meaning: to approach, to get close to
things like, stuff such as (listing particle)

grammar: 近づきすぎて uses V-stem + すぎる (too much) in て-form to chain the cause. んだよな adds an explanatory, slightly self-pitying tone. The sentence trails off with とか — Tidus is about to list things he can't remember.

text: ここがどこなのかとか / シンの毒気にやられたか
translation: …like where I am — guess I got hit by Sin's toxin.

vocabulary.meaning: to be done in, to be hit/beaten (passive/resultative)

grammar: This continues the trailing とか list from the previous clip. シンの毒気にやられたか is a rhetorical question Wakka poses to himself — 'I guess Sin's toxin got to him.' The か at the end signals conjecture, not a question directed at Tidus.

text: でも、こうして生きてるんだ / エボンの賜物だな
translation: But still, you're alive like this — that's Yevon's blessing.
grammar: 生きてるんだ uses the progressive て-form + いる (contracted to てる) + んだ for an explanatory/emphatic assertion. エボンの賜物だな is a set-phrase acknowledgement of Yevon's blessing; な adds a tone of satisfied conclusion.

text: トレーニング続けてろ
translation: Keep training.
grammar: 続けてろ is a blunt imperative: V-te form + いろ (contracted to ろ), meaning 'keep doing [it].' It's Wakka dismissing his players to continue practice while he talks to Tidus.

text: 俺はワッカ / このビサイドオーラカの選手権コーチだ
translation: I'm Wakka — coach of the Besaid Aurochs for the tournament.
grammar: Standard self-introduction with だ at the end. ビサイドオーラカ is the team name (Besaid Aurochs). 選手権コーチ functions as a compound noun modifying Wakka's role.

text: なんだ腹減りか
translation: What's this, you hungry?

vocabulary.meaning: what is it, oh I see (exclamatory)

grammar: 腹減りか is colloquial: 腹 (stomach) + 減り (stem of 減る, to decrease) + か (question). The particle が is dropped for casual speech. なんだ expresses mild surprise.

text: よし村行くぞ / なんか食わしてやる
translation: Alright, let's head to the village — I'll get you something to eat.

vocabulary.meaning: to feed (causative of 食う, to eat)
to do something for someone (often implying doing a favor, can be patronizing)

grammar: 行くぞ uses ぞ for assertive masculine emphasis — 'we're going.' 食わせてやる combines causative (食わせる) + てやる (doing for the other person), meaning 'I'll feed you' with a generously casual tone.

text: ワッカはいいやつだと思った
translation: I thought Wakka was a good guy.
grammar: 〜と思った: the と is a quotation particle marking the content of the thought. Past tense 思った indicates this is Tidus reflecting in narration.

text: だから聞いてみたくなったんだ
translation: That's why I felt like asking him.

vocabulary.meaning: to come to want to, to feel like doing

grammar: 聞いてみたくなった combines 聞く + てみる (try asking) + たくなる (come to want to). The なったんだ ending adds narration/explanation nuance. This is Tidus explaining why he brought up Zanarkand.

text: あのさザナルカンドって千年前に滅びたんだよな
translation: Hey, so Zanarkand was destroyed a thousand years ago, right?

vocabulary.meaning: to perish, to be destroyed, to fall

grammar: 〜って is a topic marker used casually for 'as for.' んだよな seeks confirmation of known information (explanatory んだ + よな for 'right?'). Tidus is testing Wakka's knowledge to understand his situation.

text: 今は遺跡になってしまったでいいんだよな
translation: And now it's become ruins — that's right, isn't it?

vocabulary.meaning: to end up doing, to have completely done (often with regret)
it's fine that, that's correct isn't it

grammar: なってしまった expresses that something has completely changed state (and laments it). でいいんだよな is a confirmation-seeking phrase: 'that's how it is, right?' Tidus is confirming what Rikku told him.

text: 昔々スピラにはでっかい街がたくさんあった
translation: Long, long ago, there were lots of huge cities in Spira.

vocabulary.meaning: huge, enormous (colloquial form of 大きい)

grammar: 昔々 is the classic Japanese story-opening formula ('Once upon a time'). Wakka begins his history lesson in a narrative register. には marks Spira as the location in which the cities existed.

text: 夜でもにぎやかに機械仕掛けの大都市だ / みんな機械の力に頼って面白おかしく遊んでたわけだ
translation: Bustling machine-driven metropolises even at night — everyone relied on the power of machines and lived it up, you see.

vocabulary.meaning: to rely on, to depend on
in an amusing and fun way, frivolously

grammar: 機械の力に頼って uses て-form to chain 'relying on machines and [then] playing.' わけだ concludes with an explanatory nuance, wrapping up the reasoning: 'that's how they lived, you see.'

text: だけどな
translation: But then…

vocabulary.meaning: sentence-final particle adding reflection or emphasis

grammar: だけどな is a dramatic pause in Wakka's narrative. The な at the end softens the contrast and creates anticipation for what comes next — a storytelling device.

text: 見てみろ / 突然シンが現れて
translation: Look at what happened — Sin suddenly appeared and…
grammar: 見てみろ is an imperative (見る + てみる + ろ) — 'just look at this.' It's a narrative device inviting the listener to imagine the scene. 現れて uses て-form to continue the action: 'Sin appeared and [then]...'

text: 機械の街を全部壊しちまった / もちろんザナルカンドもな
translation: Sin destroyed all the machine cities — Zanarkand included, of course.

vocabulary.meaning: to end up doing (colloquial contraction of てしまう)

grammar: 壊しちまった is a casual contraction of 壊してしまった — completed action with a sense of finality or regret. もちろんザナルカンドもな: the も adds 'Zanarkand too,' and な is reflective.

text: それがだいたい千年前 / お前の言う通りだ
translation: That was roughly a thousand years ago — just like you said.
grammar: それがだいたい千年前: the predicate (だ) is dropped — common in casual speech. お前の言う通りだ confirms Tidus's guess using the pattern Noun + の + Verb + 通りだ ('exactly as Noun verbed').

text: シンは調子に乗っちまった人間への罰ってわけだな
translation: Sin is a punishment for humanity getting too carried away, you see.

vocabulary.meaning: to get carried away, to become arrogant

grammar: 調子に乗っちまった is a relative clause modifying 人間 (humans who got carried away). への罰 = 'punishment toward/for.' ってわけだな wraps it up as a logical conclusion Wakka believes in as doctrine.

text: まったく / ああ、昔の奴らのせいで今の俺たちが苦労するなんて腹が立つよな
translation: Honestly… it really makes me angry that we today have to suffer because of those people from the past.

vocabulary.meaning: because of, due to (negative causation, blaming)
to suffer hardship, to have a hard time
the fact that, things like (expressing disbelief or emotion)
to get angry, to be irritated (lit. stomach stands up)

grammar: 〜のせいで assigns blame. 〜なんて adds emotional charge — disbelief or frustration at the situation. 腹が立つよな invites the listener to agree: 'it's infuriating, isn't it?'

text: もちろん罪を償うのは今の人間の大切な役目だ
translation: Of course, atoning for those sins is the important duty of people today.

vocabulary.meaning: to atone for, to make amends

grammar: 罪を償うのは nominalizes the verb phrase ('the act of atoning'). 今の人間の大切な役目だ asserts it as their duty. Wakka catches himself and adds this disclaimer — showing he accepts Yevon's doctrine despite his frustration.

text: そりゃわかってるさ、でも時々やりきれなくなってな
translation: I know that, of course — but sometimes it just gets to be too much.

vocabulary.meaning: of course, that (colloquial contraction of それは)
I know, I understand (progressive expressing ongoing state)
unbearable, can't stand it (lit. cannot carry through)

grammar: やりきれなくなって uses the adjective やりきれない → adverb form (〜く) + なる (become) + て-form, meaning 'it becomes unbearable.' The sentence ends with な in a trailing, reflective way, as if Wakka is talking to himself.

text: リュックの言った通りだった
translation: It was just as Rikku had said.
grammar: Tidus's narration confirms Rikku's earlier advice. 〜た通りだった: past tense on both verb and copula, indicating this was validated in retrospect.

text: 嘘をつく必要なんて全然ないんだ
translation: There's absolutely no need to lie.

vocabulary.meaning: to lie, to tell a lie
at all, not at all (with negative)

grammar: 必要なんて全然ないんだ: なんて after 必要 adds a dismissive nuance ('any need to lie'). 全然ない (not at all) reinforces zero necessity. んだ is explanatory — Tidus is resolving to tell the truth about Zanarkand.

text: でもよ、ザナルカンドエイブスってのは笑えたぞ
translation: But still, the Zanarkand Abes — that did make me laugh.

vocabulary.meaning: the thing called, as for (colloquial topic marker)
can laugh at, funny (potential form of 笑う)

grammar: ってのは is a casual topicalizer (= というのは). 笑えたぞ: potential past tense (could laugh) + ぞ for assertive masculine emphasis — Wakka admits Tidus's team name amused him.

text: もしかしたらそんなチーム本当にあったのかもしれないけどよ
translation: Maybe a team like that really did exist, though.

vocabulary.meaning: though, but (casual with よ for softening/hedging)

grammar: もしかしたら〜かもしれない is a doubly hedged expression of possibility. けどよ at the end softens the overall claim — Wakka is conceding the theoretical possibility while not fully believing it.

text: まあ、楽して暮らしてた時代のチームなんていわっちに決まってるけどね
translation: Well, a team from an age when people lived easy must've been weak, obviously.

vocabulary.meaning: to take it easy, to live comfortably

grammar: 楽して暮らしてた時代の is a relative clause modifying チーム. 〜に決まってる expresses strong certainty. Wakka betrays his prejudice against the machine-using era — and indirectly disparages Tidus's origins.

text: お前が落ち込むことないだろうが / 俺を励ましてくれる輪っかの気持ち、嬉しかった
translation: You've got no reason to be down about it — I was happy that Wakka was trying to cheer me up.

vocabulary.meaning: to be depressed, to feel down
to do something for me (favor received)

grammar: 落ち込むことないだろうが: ことない = 'no need to,' だろうが adds a slightly argumentative 'come on.' The second sentence is Tidus's internal narration; 励ましてくれる uses くれる to mark the favor done to Tidus.

text: でもその時、俺が考えていたのは始まりは真だ
translation: But at that moment, what I was thinking was: it all starts with Jecht.

vocabulary.meaning: at that time, at that moment

grammar: 〜が考えていたのは nominalizes 'what I was thinking.' 始まりは真だ asserts that Jecht (真) is the beginning/origin. This is Tidus pivoting to his real goal — finding Jecht to get home.

text: もう一度シーンに会えば / それができたら
translation: If I could meet Jecht once more — if that were possible…
grammar: Two parallel conditional clauses (〜ば / 〜たら) building hope. シーン likely refers to Jecht (ジェクト). Both clauses are left incomplete, trailing into the next line — a rhetorical structure of longing.

text: ザナルカンドへ帰ることができるかもしれない / その時が来るまでは
translation: Maybe I can return to Zanarkand — until that time comes…

vocabulary.meaning: can do, to be able to

grammar: 〜ことができるかもしれない: ability (できる) + possibility (かもしれない). その時が来るまでは marks the temporal limit of Tidus's resolve — 'until that moment' implying he'll endure until then.

text: ここがどこかとか / いつの時代だとか
translation: Things like where this place is, or what era it is…

vocabulary.meaning: what era, which period of time

grammar: Parallel とか listing two existential questions Tidus is choosing to set aside. The syntax mirrors the earlier clip_004 — circular structure reinforcing his mental state.

text: 気にするのはやめよう / 気にしないってのは難しかったけど
translation: I'll stop worrying about it — though not worrying was hard.
grammar: 気にするのはやめよう: の nominalizes the verb, then やめよう (volitional) expresses a decision. 気にしないってのは難しかったけど: the ってのは is a colloquial topicalizer; past tense admits the actual difficulty.

text: 少しだけ楽になった / ほんの
translation: I felt just a little bit better — just barely…

vocabulary.meaning: just a little, only a little
to feel easier, to become more comfortable

grammar: だけ limits the extent ('only a little'). 楽になった marks a change of state. ほんの trails off — it modifies 少し in the next clip. The split across two clips creates a deliberate dramatic pause.

text: 少しだけ
translation: …just a little.

vocabulary.meaning: just a little, only a little

grammar: A callback completing the trailing ほんの from clip_035. The repetition of 少しだけ separated by a pause is a deliberate emotional technique — Tidus's vulnerability in these words.

text: なんかあんのか
translation: Something up?

vocabulary.meaning: to be, to exist (for inanimate things)

grammar: あんのか is colloquial contraction of あるのか ('is there something?'). Very casual — Tidus addressing someone who has approached him.

text: 何すんだよ
translation: What are you doing?!
grammar: 何すんだよ: すんだ is a contraction of するんだ. よ at the end expresses irritation or protest. This is a sharp reaction to someone grabbing or accosting Tidus.

text: 離せよ! / お願いがあるんだなぁ…
translation: Let go! / I've got a favor to ask…

vocabulary.meaning: I have a (thing), there is a (thing) I need to

grammar: 離せよ is an imperative (離す → 離せ) + よ for strong command. お願いがあるんだなぁ: のんだ is explanatory ('I have a request'), なぁ adds a softening, pleading nuance. The ellipsis (…) suggests hesitation.

text: あんたのチームに入れてんだろ?
translation: You'll let me onto your team, right?

vocabulary.meaning: to let in, to include, to admit
you are doing/going to, right? (seeking confirmation, colloquial)

grammar: 入れてんだろ: 入れている (in the state of including/letting in) → contracted to 入れてん + だろ (surely, right?). This is Tidus's bold request to join the Aurochs.

text: もうすぐ大きなブリッツの大会がある。スピラ中のチームが集まるでかいやつだ。
translation: There's a big blitzball tournament coming up soon — a huge one where teams from all over Spira gather.
grammar: スピラ中 uses 中 as a suffix meaning 'throughout' (じゅう). でかいやつだ: やつ is a colloquial noun ('thing/one') — 'a big one.' The two sentences build from announcement to emphasis.

text: でかい大会だから、お前のこと知ってる奴らもきっと来る。
translation: Because it's a big tournament, people who know you will surely come.
grammar: 〜だから: causal connector ('because it is big'). お前のこと知ってる奴ら: relative clause modifying 奴ら. きっと adds confident expectation. Wakka is pitching this as a path home for Tidus.

text: そしたら、お前元のチームや生活に戻れるだろ?
translation: Then you'd be able to return to your old team and life, right?
grammar: そしたら is a casual conditional ('if that happens, then'). 戻れるだろ: potential form (戻れる) + だろ for confirmation-seeking. Wakka genuinely believes this plan will reunite Tidus with his people.

text: なあ、悪い話じゃないと思うぞ。どうだ? / はい。
translation: Hey, I think it's not a bad deal. What do you say? / Yes.

vocabulary.meaning: what do you think, how about it

grammar: 悪い話じゃないと思うぞ: double negative (not a bad deal) + ぞ for assertive confidence. Wakka is selling the idea. どうだ? is a direct prompt for agreement. はい is Tidus's simple acceptance.

text: ああ。
translation: Yeah.
grammar: Single-syllable affirmative typical of casual masculine Japanese speech. The minimalism signals acceptance without enthusiasm.

text: いいよ。
translation: Sure.
grammar: いいよ: いい (good/okay) + よ for light assertive agreement. A brief, friendly acceptance.

text: ありがとうよ大会まで頼んだぜ
translation: Thanks — I'm counting on you till the tournament!

vocabulary.meaning: to ask, to rely on, to count on
sentence-final particle expressing assertion or urging (masculine, casual)

grammar: 頼んだぜ: past tense of 頼む (I'm relying on you) + ぜ for masculine emphasis. In Japanese, past tense can be used for requests that are now set — 'I'm counting on you (it's settled).'

text: ブリッツとシンだけがザナルカンドとスピラを繋いでるような気がしたんだ
translation: I had a feeling that only blitzball and Sin connected Zanarkand and Spira.

vocabulary.meaning: I have a feeling that, it feels like

grammar: 〜ような気がしたんだ: ような (like, as if) + 気がする (have a feeling) + た (past) + んだ (explanation). A reflective narration — Tidus articulating his intuition that these two things are his thread home.

text: そんなに外れてなかったろ
translation: That wasn't so far off, was it.

vocabulary.meaning: to be off, to miss the mark, to be wrong

grammar: そんなに + negative: 'not that much.' 外れてなかったろ is a rhetorical confirmation seeking ('it wasn't that far off, right?'). Tidus in hindsight acknowledges his instinct was correct.

text: 俺はあそこで生まれて、5歳でブリッツボールを始めた。
translation: I was born there, and started playing blitzball at age five.
grammar: Wakka's self-introduction continues. て-form chains the two events sequentially. 5歳で uses で to mark the age at which an action took place.

text: 13歳でビサイドオーラカに入って、10年戦士ってやつだな。
translation: I joined the Besaid Aurochs at 13, so I'm a ten-year veteran, as they say.

vocabulary.meaning: warrior, veteran (here: player with years of experience)
the so-called, what you'd call (colloquial quotation)

grammar: 10年戦士ってやつだな: って quotes the label, やつ is a casual nominalizer, だな is a mild assertion. This is Wakka defining himself with rueful pride.

text: でも、10年やっても大会じゃ一度も勝てなかった。
translation: But even after ten years, I never won a single tournament.
grammar: 10年やっても: concessive て-form (even doing it for 10 years). 一度も勝てなかった: 一度も + negative potential (勝てなかった) = 'could not win even once.' The pain in this admission is central to Wakka's arc.

text: んで、引き際が肝心だってんで、去年の大会を最後に引退したんだ。
translation: So, since knowing when to quit is key, I retired after last year's tournament.

vocabulary.meaning: the right time to quit, graceful exit
because they say (colloquial: だということで)

grammar: 引き際が肝心だってんで: a colloquial contraction of 〜だということで (because it is said that). 去年の大会を最後に uses を最後に ('making X the last') — a fixed expression for retiring after a final event.

text: でな、引退してから新しい仕事を始めたんだな。 / でもちょっと気抜いたらすぐブリッツのこと考えちまう。
translation: And, since retiring I started a new job — but the moment I let my guard down, I start thinking about blitzball right away.

vocabulary.meaning: to let one's guard down, to relax attention
end up doing (colloquial てしまう)

grammar: 〜てから: 'after doing.' ちょっと気抜いたら: conditional (〜たら) — 'if I let my guard down even a little.' すぐ adds immediacy. 考えちまう: involuntary, uncontrolled tendency — Wakka can't stop thinking about blitzball.

text: 10年間勝ちなしじゃな。
translation: Ten years without a win, after all.

vocabulary.meaning: after all, indeed (reflective ending, slightly dialectal/older)

grammar: じゃな is a reflective sentence-final particle (similar to だな but slightly archaic or dialectal). The line is a grim self-summary — Wakka stating the bare fact of his record.

text: 去年の1回戦はチャンスだった。
translation: Last year's first round was a real chance.
grammar: Simple past declarative. チャンスだった: the past copula marks this as a lost opportunity — regret implied.

text: でも、きついことがあって試合に集中できなかった。
translation: But something hard happened and I couldn't concentrate on the game.
grammar: きついことがあって: nominalized adjective (きついこと = something hard) + があって (there was, causing). 集中できなかった: negative potential past (could not concentrate). Wakka is referring obliquely to his brother Chappu's death.

text: 言い訳っすね。 / 厳しいっすね。
translation: That's an excuse. / You're tough.

vocabulary.meaning: isn't it, right? (polite but casual contraction of ですね)

grammar: 〜っすね is a contraction of ですね common among younger speakers or in casual-polite registers. 言い訳っすね: Tidus bluntly calling out Wakka's excuse. 厳しいっすね: Wakka's rueful acknowledgement that Tidus is right.

text: 次の大会で勝ってスッキリしたい / そういうことか
translation: I want to win the next tournament and feel at peace — so that's what this is about.

vocabulary.meaning: to feel refreshed, to feel at peace, to have closure
so that's what it is, I see (realizing)

grammar: スッキリしたい expresses Wakka's desire for closure. そういうことか: Tidus's realization — 'Ah, so that's what's going on.' A key character moment: winning the tournament is personal redemption for Wakka.

text: 大会の目標は? / 順位は関係ないんだ
translation: What's your goal for the tournament? / Ranking doesn't matter.
grammar: 大会の目標は? is an elliptical question (verb dropped — context makes it clear). 順位は関係ないんだ: は marks 順位 as the topic being rejected; んだ is explanatory ('the thing is, ranking doesn't matter').

text: いい試合ができたらそれでいい
translation: If we can play a good game, that's enough.

vocabulary.meaning: that's fine, that's enough, that'll do

grammar: 〜たら: conditional. それでいい: a set expression meaning 'that's sufficient.' Wakka's stated goal is process over outcome — though Tidus will challenge this.

text: 本気でやったって充実感があれば / 俺スッキリやめられると思う
translation: If I gave it my all and feel fulfilled, I think I can quit with no regrets.

vocabulary.meaning: can quit after doing, able to retire having done

grammar: 本気でやったって: やった (did) + って (even if) — 'even if I gave it my all.' 充実感があれば: conditional. スッキリやめられる: スッキリ modifies やめる — 'quit cleanly/with peace.' Wakka's true wish.

text: 目標! / って聞かれたら / 優勝!
translation: Goal! / If someone asks — / Championship!
grammar: Tidus is roleplaying the answer Wakka should give. 聞かれたら: passive (聞かれる, to be asked) + たら conditional. 優勝! is the punchy, confident answer Tidus insists on — no hedging.

text: って答えろよ
translation: That's what you should answer!

vocabulary.meaning: just do it, you should (imperative + よ)

grammar: って quotes the answer 優勝. 答えろよ: imperative (答えろ) + よ for slightly exasperated insistence. Tidus is coaching Wakka on having the winning mindset.

text: 試合に出るなら勝つ / それ以外何があるんだ
translation: If you're in a game, you win — what else is there?

vocabulary.meaning: to compete in a match, to play in a game

grammar: 〜なら: conditional based on an already-given premise ('if you're going to play'). それ以外何があるんだ is rhetorical — 'what else could there possibly be?' Tidus's philosophy: play to win, period.

text: 優勝
translation: Championship.
grammar: A single word delivered flatly — Wakka reluctantly adopts Tidus's framing. No grammar needed; the power is in the minimalism.

text: マジっすか
translation: Seriously?

vocabulary.meaning: seriously, for real (from 真面目, shortened slang)

grammar: マジっすか is a casual-polite expression of disbelief or surprise. っすか contracts ですか. Used widely in contemporary informal Japanese.

text: ああ海から来た人か
translation: Ah, you're the one who came from the sea.
grammar: 海から来た人か: relative clause (came from the sea) modifying 人. か at the end marks realization or recognition — 'Oh, so you're the person who came from the sea.' A villager recognizing Tidus.

text: この道は魔物が多いから注意した方がいいよ
translation: There are lots of monsters on this path, so you should be careful.

vocabulary.meaning: to be careful, to pay attention
it is better to, you should

grammar: 〜から: causal ('because there are many monsters'). 注意した方がいいよ: 〜た方がいい is a recommendation pattern ('it would be better to have done X'). よ adds mild insistence.

text: シンに近づいたのに助かったんだろう / こんなところでやられるなよ
translation: Even though you got close to Sin and survived — don't go getting done in here of all places.

vocabulary.meaning: even though, despite (expressing contrast or surprise)
to be beaten, to be done in

grammar: のに expresses ironic contrast — surviving Sin only to die to a common monster. やられるなよ: negative imperative with よ for friendly warning ('don't get beaten'). な before よ is the prohibitive particle.

text: 誰
translation: Who?
grammar: A bare interrogative — minimal, suspicious. Someone (likely Lulu or Kimahri) responding curtly to Tidus's approach.

text: ん?討伐隊? / お前、そんなことも忘れちまったのか?
translation: Hmm? The extermination squad? / You've even forgotten something like that?

vocabulary.meaning: extermination squad, subjugation unit (a Sin-fighting group)
to end up (colloquial てしまう)

grammar: 討伐隊? is a bare noun question — Wakka is surprised Tidus doesn't know the term. そんなことも忘れちまったのか: のか is a questioning/surprised nominalizer ending ('you've actually forgotten?'). も adds 'even this.'

text: 悪かった。気にすんな。俺が面倒見てやる。
translation: My bad. Don't worry about it. I'll look after you.

vocabulary.meaning: I'm sorry, my bad (past adj. as apology)
to look after, to take care of

grammar: 悪かった as a standalone apology (lit. 'it was bad' = 'I was wrong'). 気にすんな: colloquial prohibitive (するな → すんな). 面倒見てやる: てやる marks the favor done from Wakka to Tidus — 'I'll take care of you.'

text: うっす。その代わり、大会の時は大活躍してやるから。
translation: Sure thing. In return, I'll put on a great show at the tournament.

vocabulary.meaning: yes, sure (casual, slightly deferential masculine acknowledgement)
to perform brilliantly, to be very active/successful

grammar: うっす is a young masculine casual affirmative. その代わり sets up a reciprocal condition. 大活躍してやるから: てやる (doing for someone) + から (because/so). Tidus confidently promising his value to the team.

text: うっす。 / ああ、討伐隊のことは直接聞けよ。村の宿舎にいるはずだ。
translation: Sure. / Oh, ask the extermination squad directly. They should be at the village lodgings.

vocabulary.meaning: should be, supposed to be (expectation based on reasoning)

grammar: 直接聞けよ: imperative (聞け) + よ for a helpful directive. 〜はずだ expresses logical expectation — Wakka knows where the squad stays. Tidus still wants to learn about the discussion squad he heard about.

text: ビサイド村だ / 食べ物ある?
translation: It's Besaid Village. / Is there food?
grammar: ビサイド村だ: simple declarative — they've arrived. 食べ物ある?: elliptical question with ある (is there?) — the か is dropped in casual speech. Tidus is hungry and not shy about it.

text: 後であの家で食わしてやる / しばらく暇つぶしてろ
translation: I'll feed you at that house later — kill some time for a bit.

vocabulary.meaning: to kill time, to pass time

grammar: 食わしてやる: alternative causative form (食わす) + てやる (doing for). しばらく暇つぶしてろ: 暇つぶす in command form + ろ (informal imperative) — 'just hang around for a while.'

text: そうだな / あそこが討伐退宿舎だ
translation: Let me see… that over there is the extermination squad's barracks.

vocabulary.meaning: let me think, well (used as a thoughtful pause)

vocabulary.reading: とうばつたいしゅくしゃ

grammar: そうだな as an opener signals Wakka pausing to think or orient Tidus. あそこが + X + だ: a locating sentence — 'that place over there is X.'

text: ルツとガッタに色々聞いてみろよ
translation: Ask Luzzu and Gatta all sorts of things.
grammar: 聞いてみろよ: 聞く + てみる (try asking) + ろ (imperative) + よ (for light insistence). Wakka directing Tidus to two Crusader soldiers (ルツ/Luzzu and ガッタ/Gatta) for information about the Crusaders.

text: そうそう / な、なんだよ? / お前、いくらなんてもお祈りは覚えてるな?
translation: Right, right. / H-hey, what is it? / You at least remember how to pray, don't you?

vocabulary.meaning: no matter what, at the very least, even so

grammar: いくらなんでも expresses 'even if nothing else' — Wakka assumes Tidus must at least know how to pray. The も here is concessive. The sentence-final な is a soft rhetorical question tag seeking confirmation.

text: 祈ったことなんてなかったから、もちろん全然知らなかった / きっと忘れてるだけだよな。まあ、とにかく教えてやる
translation: I had never prayed before, so of course I had no idea. / You've just forgotten, I'm sure. Well, anyway, I'll teach you.
grammar: 〜てやる (教えてやる) is a benefactive form meaning 'I'll do ~ for you,' often carrying a slightly condescending or magnanimous nuance — Wakka is generously offering to teach Tidus. The first half is Tidus's internal monologue (past tense); the second is Wakka's spoken line.

text: ほれ、やってみ?
translation: Go on, give it a try.

vocabulary.meaning: here, come on, go ahead (casual prompt)

grammar: やってみ is a casual contracted imperative of やってみろ/やってみて — Wakka is urging Tidus to attempt the prayer gesture. ほれ is a dialectal/casual version of ほら.

text: ん、うん
translation: Mm, yeah.
grammar: A minimal utterance — Tidus's hesitant acknowledgment before attempting the prayer. The double filler (ん、うん) shows uncertainty or reluctance.

text: よし!上出来だ!
translation: Alright! Well done!

vocabulary.meaning: well done, excellent result, good job

grammar: よし is an interjection expressing approval. 上出来だ uses the noun 上出来 (fine result) with copula だ — Wakka praises Tidus's first attempt at the Yevon prayer.

text: じゃあ寺院の召喚師様にご挨拶してきな
translation: Now then, go pay your respects to the summoner at the temple.
grammar: してきな is a casual imperative form of してくる — 'go and do (and come back).' The prefix ご on 挨拶 is a politeness marker. 召喚師様 uses さま to show reverence for the summoner.

text: それは… / 勝利のおまじないだった
translation: That was… / a good-luck charm for victory.
grammar: Tidus's internal monologue realizing the Yevon prayer gesture is the same as his team's pre-game ritual. The ellipsis (…) shows dawning recognition. だった is past copula — 'it was.'

text: なんか本当に俺の知らない世界だった
translation: It was truly a world I knew nothing about.
grammar: 俺の知らない世界 is a noun phrase: 知らない (attributive negative) modifies 世界, and 俺の marks the subject of that relative clause. だった is past copula. なんか softens the statement — Tidus is processing the unfamiliarity of Spira.

text: ブラスカ様が大召喚師となられてから10年
translation: Ten years have passed since Lord Braska became High Summoner.
grammar: となられて is the honorific form of となって (て-form of となる). The 〜てから structure marks a temporal starting point: 'from the time he became ~ / since he became ~.' The sentence has no main verb — it's a nominal/incomplete sentence functioning as a heading or preamble.

text: やっとこの寺院にもご聖像が届きました
translation: At last, the sacred statue has arrived even at this temple.

vocabulary.meaning: to arrive, to be delivered, to reach

grammar: も after 寺院に adds an inclusive nuance — 'even to this temple.' やっと conveys that this arrival was long-awaited. ご is an honorific prefix on 聖像, reflecting the statue's religious significance.

text: 大召喚師ってなんすか?
translation: What's a High Summoner?
grammar: って is a casual quotation/topic marker equivalent to とは. なんすか is a colloquial contraction of なんですか (polite question). Tidus genuinely doesn't know this term — another marker of his outsider status.

text: なっ あの 俺 真の毒気に当たっちゃったんです
translation: Uh — um, I got hit by Sin's toxin, you see.

vocabulary.meaning: to be hit by, to be struck by, to be exposed to

grammar: 当たっちゃったんです combines 当たる + てしまった (contracted to ちゃった) + んです (explanatory). This is Tidus's standard excuse for not knowing things. ちゃった adds the nuance of an unfortunate mishap.

text: 何度も同じ言い訳をする自分が 少しおかしくて 寂しかった
translation: I found myself a little ridiculous — and lonely — for making the same excuse over and over.
grammar: する自分 is a relative clause nominalizing Tidus's own behavior ('the self who keeps making…'). おかしくて uses the て-form to coordinate adjectives: 'ridiculous AND lonely.' This is introspective internal monologue.

text: 召喚師とは 神秘の技で 我らエヴォンの民をお守りくださるお方
translation: A summoner is one who protects us, the people of Yevon, with mysterious arts.

vocabulary.meaning: to protect/guard (honorific, receiving the favor of)

grammar: 〜とは defines a concept: 'as for what a summoner is…' お守りくださる is an honorific form showing the summoner bestows protection on the people. お方 (vs. 人) signals reverence. The sentence has no explicit copula — formal/ritual speech.

text: 選ばれし召喚師が操るは、血肉を持たざる聖なる獣、召喚獣。
translation: What the chosen summoner commands are sacred beasts without flesh and blood — the aeons.

vocabulary.meaning: to control, to command, to manipulate
not possessing (archaic negative attributive of 持つ)

grammar: 選ばれし uses an archaic attributive form (classical 〜し instead of modern 〜た). 持たざる is classical negative attributive (〜ざる = 〜ない in modern). The whole passage uses elevated, liturgical register appropriate to a religious recitation.

text: 祈りに応えて姿を現す召喚獣は、大いなるエボンの賜物。
translation: The aeons who appear in answer to prayer are a great gift of Yevon.

vocabulary.meaning: to appear, to manifest one's form

grammar: 大いなる is an archaic attributive form of 大いに (greatly). 賜物 carries religious/divine connotation — a gift granted by a higher power. The sentence ends nominally (no verb) in formal declarative style.

text: 要するに、なんだかすごいおじさんたちに感謝しなさいってことだと思った。
translation: In short, I figured it basically meant: be grateful to some amazing old guys.

vocabulary.meaning: in short, to sum up, basically
somehow, for some reason, sort of
middle-aged man, uncle (informal for older men)
to be grateful, to give thanks
it means that ~, it comes down to ~

grammar: Tidus humorously reduces the formal religious speech to plain terms. 〜ってことだ condenses and rephrases — 'it amounts to ~.' と思った marks this as his personal interpretation. The comedic contrast between the ornate liturgy and his casual summary is intentional.

text: 悪いなぁ 飯はまだなんだ / 昼寝でもしてろ 疲れてるんだろ?
translation: Sorry about that — food's not ready yet. / Take a nap or something. You're tired, right?

vocabulary.meaning: go ahead and do ~ or something (casual suggestion/command)
to get tired, to be tired

grammar: 悪いなぁ is a casual apology (short for 悪いな = sorry). 飯はまだなんだ — the んだ gives an explanatory nuance ('the thing is, food isn't ready'). でもしてろ uses でも (or something like that) + imperative してろ for a casual suggestion.

text: 様子を見に行った方が良くはなかろうか? / うーん、大丈夫だと思うんですが
translation: Shouldn't we go check on her? / Hmm, I think she's all right, but…

vocabulary.meaning: to check on someone, to see how things are
it would be better to ~, ought to ~

grammar: なかろうか is a formal/archaic rhetorical question: 'wouldn't it be better to ~?' The second speaker's response ends with が, leaving the sentence open — implying a mild concession or reservation ('I think it's fine, but…').

text: しかし、もうかれこれ
translation: But, it's already been quite some time…
grammar: The sentence is incomplete — cut off before the time period is stated. This mirrors real speech where the sentence is interrupted or trails off. かれこれ is typically followed by a time duration.

text: しかし、もうかれこれ
translation: But, it's already been quite some time…
grammar: Repeated from the previous clip — the same worried statement is interrupted again, emphasizing the speaker's mounting anxiety about the summoner's prolonged absence.

text: かれこれ、一日経っているからな
translation: It's been a whole day already, after all.
grammar: 経っている is the progressive/stative of 経つ — 'time has elapsed and the situation continues.' からな is a casual explanatory ending meaning 'because that's the case' or 'after all.' Expresses the speaker's justification for concern.

text: 様子を見に行ってもらえますか?
translation: Could you please go and check on her?

vocabulary.meaning: to check on, to see how things are

grammar: 〜てもらえますか is a polite request form using the potential of もらう: 'could I receive the favor of your going to check?' It's softer and more indirect than an imperative.

text: すでに関係者で手分けして探している
translation: Those involved are already searching in groups.

vocabulary.meaning: to divide the work, to split up and search
to search for, to look for

grammar: 手分けして is the te-form of 手分けする, used adverbially: 'dividing up and [then] searching.' The て-form chains actions. すでに emphasizes it's already underway — the speaker is reassuring the worried party.

text: ありがとうございます
translation: Thank you very much.

vocabulary.word: ありがとうございます
vocabulary.reading: ありがとうございます

grammar: Standard polite expression of gratitude. The formal ございます form (vs. casual ありがとう) signals the speaker is addressing someone of higher status or in a formal situation.

text: あんなやつ帰ってこなくてもいいのに
translation: I don't care if someone like that never comes back.

vocabulary.meaning: someone like that, a person of that sort (dismissive)
it's fine not to ~, doesn't have to ~
even though ~, I wish ~ (expresses discontent or unmet desire)

grammar: 〜のに at the end of a declarative sentence expresses the speaker's frustrated wish or complaint: 'it would be fine if they didn't come back, and yet here we are worrying.' The tone is bitter and dismissive — this character has deep resentment toward whoever is inside.

text: 死んでしまうかもしれないのよ / それでもいい
translation: They might die, you know. / That's fine with me.

vocabulary.meaning: to end up doing ~, (expressing regret or finality)
you know, I'm telling you (feminine sentence-final)
that's fine, even so it's okay

grammar: 〜のよ is a feminine sentence-final particle adding emphasis or emotional explanation. The shocking それでもいい ('even that is okay') reveals intense resentment — this character would rather the person inside die than return.

text: そんなに
translation: That much?

vocabulary.meaning: that much, to that extent, so (much)

grammar: A two-word exclamation expressing disbelief at the intensity of the sentiment. The sentence is incomplete — the listener is stunned and trails off, unable to finish the question.

text: そんなにお父さんが嫌い
translation: You hate your father that much?

vocabulary.meaning: that much, to such a degree

grammar: This is a question without a question marker — the rising intonation and context make it interrogative. Completing the stunned fragment from the previous line, the speaker finally forms the full question.

text: 死んでしまったら
translation: If they were to die—

vocabulary.meaning: if ~ were to happen (with sense of finality/regret)

grammar: 〜たら is a conditional. 〜てしまったら adds the nuance of an irreversible or regrettable outcome. The sentence is left incomplete — the consequence is implied but not stated, leaving it hanging emotionally.

text: 嫌いだってことも伝えられないのよ
translation: Then I couldn't even tell them how much I hate them.

vocabulary.meaning: to convey, to tell, to communicate

grammar: Completing the conditional from the previous line: 'if they died, I couldn't even convey that I hate them.' This reveals a complex emotion — hatred mixed with an unmet need to express it. 〜だってこと nominalization makes 'my hatred' the object of 伝える.

text: で、自由召喚士はそのさらに奥で祈る。
translation: And the summoner candidate prays even deeper within.

vocabulary.meaning: apprentice/candidate summoner (lit. 'free summoner,' one seeking fayth approval)
the inner area, back, deeper within

grammar: さらに奥 — さらに intensifies 奥 ('even deeper inside'). で is a casual connective ('and, then'). This is someone explaining the structure of the Cloister of Trials to Tidus.

text: 祈りが通じれば正式な召喚士になれるって、思い出したな。
translation: If the prayer is answered, they can become a full-fledged summoner — I remembered that.

vocabulary.meaning: to get through, to be heard, to work

grammar: 〜れば is a conditional: 'if the prayer is heard.' 〜って quotes the content remembered. 思い出したな — な at the end is a self-directed reflective particle ('I remembered, huh'). Tidus piecing together how the summoner system works.

text: 誰かが奥の奥から帰ってこない。それは分かった。
translation: Someone hasn't come back from the very deepest part. That much was clear.

vocabulary.meaning: the very inner depths, deepest part

grammar: Two short declarative sentences. 奥の奥 is a reduplication for emphasis — 'the very deepest of the deep.' 帰ってこない uses くる (directional — coming back toward the speaker's location) with negative. それは分かった — concise acknowledgment of what Tidus has grasped.

text: もう一日経っちまった。 / 命に関わること、なのか?
translation: A whole day has already passed. / Could it be a matter of life and death?

vocabulary.meaning: ended up ~ (casual contraction of 〜てしまった)
to be a matter of life and death, to concern one's life

grammar: 経っちまった is casual spoken contraction of 経ってしまった — 'time has gone by (unfortunately).' 命に関わること — こと nominalizes the phrase. なのか at the end asks a genuine question with の (explanatory) + か (question marker), expressing dawning worry.

text: 時には、な。 / どうして助けに行かない?
translation: Sometimes, yes. / Then why don't you go help?
grammar: 時には、な is a minimal, reluctant confirmation — 'yes, sometimes [it is].' な here is a reflective masculine sentence-final particle. The second line is a direct question from Tidus, logically following: if it can be fatal, why just stand by?

text: ちゃんとガードがついてるし、何より掟だし
translation: There's a proper guardian with her, and above all, it's the law.
grammar: Two clauses joined by し, which lists concurrent reasons: 'X is the case, and Y is the case.' し is used when giving multiple reasons for something. 何より places the second reason (the rule) above the first in importance.

text: もしものことあったらどうすんだよ!死んじまったらおしまいだろ!
translation: What if something happens?! If she dies, that's it, it's over!

vocabulary.meaning: the worst case, something terrible happening (euphemism for death/disaster)
what to do, what will happen
ended up ~ (casual contraction of 〜てしまった)

grammar: Tidus erupts in frustration. もしものこと is a common euphemism for something terrible or fatal. どうすんだよ — すん is a colloquial contraction of する; だよ adds exasperation. 死んじまったら is casual: 死んでしまったら (conditional). おしまいだろ — だろ is a forceful rhetorical tag.

text: 掟を破ってはなりません!
translation: You must not break the law!

vocabulary.meaning: must not ~, it is not permitted to ~

grammar: 〜てはなりません is a strong formal prohibition: 'it is not allowed to ~.' More formal and authoritative than 〜てはいけない. The stern official is shutting down Tidus's emotional outburst with an appeal to rules.

text: 死ぬか!
translation: She could die!
grammar: A bare exclamatory outburst — か here is not a neutral question but an emotional exclamation conveying disbelief and urgency. Tidus is shouting that death is the issue. The brevity amplifies the emotional intensity.

text: いきなり、心細くなった
translation: All of a sudden, I felt anxious and alone.

vocabulary.meaning: suddenly, all at once, without warning
feeling lonely and anxious, uneasy, insecure

grammar: 心細くなった — 心細い (adjective) → 心細く (adverbial/conjunctive form) + なった (became). Tidus's internal monologue capturing a sudden emotional vulnerability after the heated confrontation. The abruptness of いきなり mirrors the unexpected feeling.

text: おい! / 何熱くなってたんだ?
translation: Hey! / What were you getting so worked up about?

vocabulary.meaning: to get worked up, to get heated/excited (figurative)

grammar: 熱くなってたんだ — 〜てた is the casual spoken contraction of 〜ていた. んだ adds a seeking-explanation nuance. Wakka arrives and casually asks what the commotion was, unaware of the tension.

text: まあ、いいや。 / ここは召喚士と銃召喚士、そしてガード以外立ち入り禁止だ。
translation: Well, never mind. / This area is off-limits to anyone other than summoners, apprentice summoners, and guardians.

vocabulary.meaning: oh well, never mind, forget it
apprentice summoner (those not yet fully consecrated)

grammar: まあいいや is a set phrase for dropping a subject. 〜以外 creates an exception clause: 'other than X.' 立ち入り禁止 is a compound noun used as a predicate here — 'entry is prohibited.'

text: 掟だからよく覚えとけ / あんたはいいのか
translation: It's the law, so remember it well. / But you're okay to be here?

vocabulary.meaning: to remember, to keep in mind

grammar: 覚えとけ is a casual imperative contraction of 覚えておけ (覚えておく → imperative). だから gives the reason. あんたはいいのか — のか here is a genuine question seeking confirmation: 'is it okay for you [to be here]?'

text: 俺はガードだからな
translation: Because I'm a guardian.
grammar: Wakka's brief self-explanation. だからな — から gives reason, な is a casual sentence-final that softens and makes it more conversational. He's simply stating his status as justification for his access.

text: ガードってば
translation: A guardian, he says…

vocabulary.meaning: speaking of ~, I said ~ (repeating with mild exasperation or surprise)

grammar: ってば is used to echo something just said, often with mild surprise, exasperation, or teasing: 'he says he's a guardian, of all things.' Here it's likely Tidus processing — slightly amazed that Wakka is actually a guardian.

text: 召喚師はスピラジュの寺院で祈りを捧げるための旅に出るんだ
translation: Summoners set out on a journey to offer prayers at the temples of Spira.

vocabulary.meaning: for the purpose of ~, in order to ~
to set out on a journey, to depart on a trip

grammar: 〜ための is a purpose modifier: 'a journey for the purpose of praying.' 旅に出るんだ — んだ adds the explanatory/informing nuance. Wakka is explaining the summoner's pilgrimage to Tidus.

text: ガードってのはその護衛だ
translation: A guardian is their escort.

vocabulary.meaning: as for what ~ is, speaking of ~ (casual definition)

grammar: 〜ってのは is a casual spoken form of 〜というのは — used to define or explain a term. Its function here is definitional: 'as for what a guardian is — it's their escort.' Short, direct explanation.

text: 今この奥にいるガードは、一人がすぐに怒るし、もう一人が何考えてるかわからん
translation: The guardians inside right now — one gets angry easily, and I can't tell what the other one is thinking.

vocabulary.meaning: one more person, the other one
I don't know, can't tell (casual negative)

grammar: し is used twice to list simultaneous traits. わからん is a casual contraction of わからない — Wakka is informally describing Lulu (quick to anger) and Kimahri (inscrutable). The character portraits are concise but vivid.

text: ま、ここまで来ちまったら一緒だもんな
translation: Well, now that we've come this far, we're in this together.

vocabulary.meaning: this far, up to this point
now that ~ has happened (casual, with finality)

grammar: 来ちまったら — casual contraction of 来てしまったら (conditional of a completed action). もんな is a casual combination of もの (explanatory) + な (seeking agreement): 'it's that kind of situation, right?' Wakka is accepting the situation pragmatically.

text: シャネ、行くぞ
translation: Shaney, let's go.
grammar: ぞ is a masculine sentence-final particle expressing strong assertion or rallying. Wakka is decisively calling to his companion and heading in to check on the summoner. シャネ is a character's name (a Besaid villager).

text: なんであんたが来るわけ?
translation: Why are you coming along?

vocabulary.meaning: reason, what's the deal (seeking justification, informal)

grammar: 〜わけ at the end of a question asks for an explanation or reason: 'what's your reasoning for coming?' Slightly confrontational — likely Lulu questioning Tidus's presence in a restricted area.

text: 私たちじゃ、不安だった? / いや、その…ついに…
translation: Were you worried about just us? / No, it's just that… well…

vocabulary.meaning: finally, at last (here used as hesitation before explanation)

grammar: 私たちじゃ — じゃ here is a casual form of では, implying 'with just us two.' The question implies Wakka doubted their ability to handle it. The response trails into ellipsis — Wakka is flustered and can't articulate his real reason for coming.

text: ほら、やっぱり怒ったろうね
translation: See? She got angry, just like I said.

vocabulary.meaning: see, look, told you (drawing attention to something)
as expected, just as I thought, after all
she probably did ~, right? (gentle confirmation of prediction)

grammar: やっぱり confirms a prior expectation. 怒ったろうね — たろう is a casual form of ただろう (past conjecture); ね seeks agreement. Likely Wakka's companion told him in advance that Lulu would react badly.

text: 召喚師は大丈夫なのか?
translation: Is the summoner all right?

vocabulary.meaning: is it ~ ? (question with の for explanation-seeking nuance)

grammar: なのか combines の (adding a seeking-explanation nuance) with か (question marker). The の here suggests Tidus wants to understand the situation, not just get a yes/no. He's genuinely concerned.

text: あんた…誰?
translation: Who… are you?
grammar: The ellipsis (…) before 誰 creates a beat of surprise or cautious curiosity. This is likely Yuna's first line to Tidus — a simple, direct question. The split structure (あんた… 誰?) mimics hesitant real speech.

text: こっちこっち!
translation: Over here, over here!

vocabulary.meaning: this way, over here (casual form of こちら)

grammar: Repetition of こっち for emphasis and urgency — 'hurry, this way!' Typical excited or urgent beckoning in casual speech.

text: な、うっ、なに? / よく見てろよ!
translation: Wha— ugh, what?! / Pay close attention!
grammar: 見てろよ is a casual imperative: 見ていろ (keep watching) contracted to 見てろ, with よ for emphasis. The first speaker is startled (な、うっ), while the second is commanding attention — probably during a blitzball demonstration.

text: 見えんねっつの!
translation: I said I can't see it!

vocabulary.meaning: to be visible, to be able to see

grammar: 見えん is a casual/dialect negative of 見える (can't see). ねっつの is a highly colloquial expression of frustrated repetition, roughly meaning 'I keep saying!' or 'that's what I told you!' It expresses exasperation at not being heard.

text: いいぞ!
translation: Nice one!
grammar: ぞ adds masculine assertiveness to いい (good). いいぞ is a standard exclamation of encouragement or praise — like 'there you go!' during a demonstration or practice.

text: はい!
translation: Yes!

vocabulary.meaning: yes; also an exclamation when scoring/achieving something

grammar: Used here as an exclamation of success or response — not just a polite 'yes' but an energetic affirmation, likely during blitzball training or a game moment.

text: おぉー!
translation: Ohhh!

vocabulary.meaning: wow, oh! (exclamation of awe or amazement)

grammar: Pure exclamatory utterance — no grammatical structure. The elongated vowel conveys awe. Likely the crowd or Tidus reacting to Yuna's summoning.

text: すごい!
translation: Amazing!
grammar: すごい used as a standalone exclamation without a topic or verb — common in spoken Japanese to express awe or admiration. One of the most versatile and frequently used exclamatory adjectives.

text: 圧倒的な光景だった / 見た目は少し怖かったけど
translation: It was an overwhelming sight. / Though the appearance was a little frightening.
grammar: Two clauses in contrast — だった (past copula) states the fact, while けど (but) introduces a concessive contrast. Tidus's internal monologue as he processes his first sight of an aeon. The balanced structure: 'it was X, but also Y.'

text: なんていうのかな / 不しぎな優しさみたいなものが
translation: How should I put it… something like a mysterious gentleness

vocabulary.meaning: how should I put it, what would you call it (thinking aloud)

grammar: なんていうのかな is a hesitation phrase used when searching for words — 'how to put it?' The sentence is incomplete (the subject 〜が has no predicate stated), continuing into the next clip. みたいなもの softens the description, hedging with 'something like.'

text: 俺にも似たわってきたんだ
translation: Washed over me too.

vocabulary.meaning: to me too, also to me
to be transmitted, to come through, to reach
to come to ~, to start to ~ (gradual change coming toward speaker)

grammar: 似たわってきた appears to be a rendering of 伝わってきた (came through, washed over) — the aeon's feeling reaching Tidus. てくる indicates movement/feeling coming toward the speaker. んだ adds a personal, reflective explanatory nuance.

text: そうそう / 初めて話をしたのは
translation: Right, right… / The first time we spoke was—

vocabulary.meaning: right right, that's right, yes yes
to have a conversation, to talk

grammar: 〜のは nominalizes the clause 初めて話をした, making it the topic: 'as for when we first talked…' The sentence is incomplete — Tidus pauses before finishing the thought, building anticipation. そうそう is a self-directed memory cue.

text: 夜になってからだった / 俺には分かってなかったけど
translation: It was after nightfall. / Though I didn't realize it at the time,
grammar: 夜になってからだった — 〜てから + だった places the conversation specifically after nightfall. 俺には分かってなかった — には marks the experiencer ('for me'), and 〜てなかった is casual spoken contraction of 〜ていなかった (was not understanding/aware).

text: あれは
translation: That was—

vocabulary.meaning: that, that thing (referring to something previously in mind)

grammar: A dramatic pause — あれは sets up the following revelation. The topic is established (that night) but the predicate is withheld, creating anticipation. In narration, this functions as a narrative breath before a significant statement.

text: 特別な夜だったんだよな / みんなの
translation: A special night — for everyone.

vocabulary.meaning: it was ~, you know (reflective past, seeking shared feeling)

grammar: だったんだよな — んだ (explanatory) + よ (assertion) + な (reflective agreement-seeking). This triple ending is very common in emotional internal monologue — Tidus is reflecting with warmth. みんなの is appended as an afterthought, expanding the significance to all.

text: 俺の
translation: Mine.
grammar: A single-word fragment for dramatic emphasis — following みんなの (everyone's), Tidus adds 俺の (mine) as a separate beat, making it personal and intimate. The rhythm mirrors the narration style of the opening.

text: チームのみんなに紹介だ / 今度の大会にどうしても出たいってんでチームに入れることになった
translation: Let me introduce you to the team. / He insisted on playing in the next tournament, so it was decided he'd join the team.

vocabulary.meaning: this time, next time, the upcoming
no matter what, absolutely, at all costs
because he said ~, saying that ~ (casual reported speech)
it was decided that ~, it came about that ~

grammar: 〜ってんで is a casual contraction of 〜と言うので (because he said ~). 〜ことになった indicates a decision was reached (often by circumstances or others), softer than 〜ことにした (a personal decision). Wakka is introducing Tidus to the blitzball team.

text: ちょっと記憶がねじ曲がってるから変なこと言うかもしれないが気にするな
translation: His memory is a bit twisted, so he might say some strange things — don't mind him.

vocabulary.meaning: to be twisted, to be warped, to be distorted
to mind, to worry about, to care about

grammar: Wakka covers for Tidus with this characteristically warm excuse. から gives the reason (twisted memory → may say odd things). 気にするな is a casual negative imperative: 'don't worry about it.' ねじ曲がってる (progressive state) vividly describes Tidus's 'confused' state.

text: 俺挨拶
translation: My turn to introduce myself.
grammar: A bare two-word utterance — no verb, no particles. This telegraphic style is typical of casual, moment-to-moment inner narration or quick spoken cues. Tidus is noting 'my introduction [follows].'

text: よろしくなみんな
translation: Nice to meet you all.

vocabulary.meaning: nice to meet you, please treat me well (standard greeting)

grammar: よろしくな is a casual masculine form of よろしく (お願いします implied). みんな is appended as an address term. The tone is confident and friendly — Tidus introducing himself to the team.

text: で大会の目標は / 精一杯頑張る
translation: And as for the tournament goal… / To give it everything I've got.

vocabulary.meaning: with all one's might, to the best of one's ability, all out
to do one's best, to persevere, to try hard

grammar: 目標は sets up the topic. 精一杯頑張る is a plain form used as a goal statement — 'to do my absolute best.' This is Tidus's initial answer before Wakka corrects him to say '優勝!' (championship).

text: 俺たちの目標は変わった / 目標は優勝だ
translation: Our goal has changed. / The goal is to win the championship.

vocabulary.meaning: championship, first place, winning the tournament

grammar: 変わった is past tense of 変わる — the goal has already changed. 目標は優勝だ is a simple copula statement: 'the goal = championship.' The abrupt declaration, after Tidus's softer answer, shows Wakka asserting a decisive shift in team ambition.

text: クリスタルの優勝カップをこの島に持ち帰る / 出る試合には全部勝つ / よそのチームは全部倒す
translation: Bring the Crystal Cup back to this island. / Win every match we enter. / Defeat every other team.

vocabulary.meaning: to bring back, to carry back
to defeat, to knock down, to beat

grammar: Three parallel plain-form statements functioning as battle proclamations. 出る試合には — には marks the scope ('in all matches that we enter'). The parallel structure and plain form give these lines a speech/rallying cry quality.

text: そうすれば優勝できる / 簡単なもんだ
translation: Do that and we'll win the championship. / Simple as that.

vocabulary.meaning: if we do that, if that's the case
that's how it is, it's simple (explanatory, colloquial)

grammar: そうすれば is a conditional: 'if we do so.' もんだ is a colloquial contraction of ものだ, here used to state something as obvious or self-evident. Wakka is humorously presenting his strategy as straightforward.

text: 優勝だ / 優勝だ / 優勝だ / 優勝だ
translation: Championship! / Championship! / Championship! / Championship!
grammar: Chanted repetition of 優勝だ — the team rallying around the single goal. The repetition is a call-and-response or group chant pattern. だ is the plain copula asserting this as their declared purpose.

text: 優勝だ
translation: We won!
grammar: Short exclamatory sentence using the plain copula だ to declare a fact with excitement. No subject is stated — it is implied from context (we / the team).

text: 優勝だ!優勝、優勝、優勝だ!
translation: We won! Victory! Victory! Victory!
grammar: Repetition of 優勝 builds emotional intensity — a common pattern in Japanese for expressing excitement or disbelief. The word is used both as a standalone exclamation and in the copular construction 優勝だ.

text: 起きて、破りめ! / 召喚師様に近づくでない! / 行けないんです!
translation: Get up, you scoundrel! / Don't get close to Lady Summoner! / I can't go!

vocabulary.meaning: get up (て-form of 起きる, used as a command)
to approach, to get close to

grammar: 〜でない is an older, stiff negative imperative used by NPCs with a traditional or guard-like register — more formal than するな. 行けないんです uses んです to express an explanation or protest ('the reason I can't go is...').

text: リューナ様、行かんぞ! / でも、元はと言えば私のせいですから…
translation: Lady Yuna, you mustn't go! / But, when you get down to it, it's my fault, so…

vocabulary.meaning: must not go, won't go (negative volitional/dialectal form of 行く)
when you trace it back to the origin, fundamentally, when you get down to it

grammar: 行かんぞ uses the dialectal/emphatic negative 〜ん (from 〜ない) with ぞ for assertion — 'you absolutely must not go.' 元はと言えば is a set phrase meaning 'if we trace things back to the root.' The trailing から… leaves the sentence incomplete, suggesting hesitation or self-blame.

text: ユーナです / さっきはありがとうございました
translation: I'm Yuna. / Thank you for what you did just now.

vocabulary.meaning: just now, a little while ago

vocabulary.word: ありがとうございました
vocabulary.reading: ありがとうございました
vocabulary.meaning: thank you very much (past tense, for something already done)

grammar: ありがとうございました uses the past tense to thank someone for a completed action — more natural than ございます when the favor has already happened. さっきは sets the time frame: 'for what happened earlier.'

text: ああ、助けに行ったことか / でもさ、あれまずかったんだろ? / 俺、余計なことしちゃったやな
translation: Oh, you mean when I came to help? / But that was a bad move, wasn't it? / I went and did something unnecessary, huh.

vocabulary.meaning: to go to help, to go to the rescue
went and did, ended up doing (expresses regret or unintended result)
huh, right? (Okinawan/Wakka's dialect for よな)

grammar: 助けに行ったこと nominalizes the verb phrase into a noun clause — 'the act of going to help.' しちゃった (してしまった) conveys that the action was unintended or regrettable. やな is Wakka's dialect, equivalent to standard よな, seeking light confirmation.

text: いいの、私が未熟だったから
translation: It's fine. It was because I was still inexperienced.

vocabulary.meaning: it's fine, it's okay (feminine soft assertion)

grammar: いいの uses the の sentence-final particle in a feminine assertive register — softly brushing aside an apology. 私が未熟だったから gives the reason using past-tense copula + から (because). The sentence ends there, leaving the conclusion implied: 'so there's no need to blame yourself.'

text: ああ、あのさ、召喚獣見たぞ / すごかった!
translation: Oh, hey — I saw your aeon! / It was incredible!
grammar: 見たぞ uses the masculine emphatic particle ぞ — Tidus asserting what he witnessed with energy. すごかった is the past tense of the い-adjective すごい, expressing how impressive it was.

text: 本当?
translation: Really?
grammar: 本当? is a one-word question using rising intonation. The か particle is dropped — extremely common in casual spoken Japanese. Yuna expresses pleasant surprise at hearing this.

text: 私、大召喚士になれると思う?
translation: Do you think I can become a great summoner?

vocabulary.meaning: can become (potential form of なる)

grammar: なれると思う? embeds the potential verb なれる inside a と思う question: 'Do you think [I] can become?' The subject 私 is stated for emphasis/clarity but は is dropped — informal and slightly vulnerable in tone, reflecting Yuna's honest self-doubt.

text: ユーナ様、もっとお話ししようよ!
translation: Lady Yuna, let's talk some more!

vocabulary.meaning: to talk, to have a conversation (polite form of 話す)

grammar: しようよ is the volitional form + よ — a warm, encouraging invitation ('let's!'). お話しする uses the honorific お prefix on 話す, showing respect toward Yuna even in casual suggestion.

text: じゃあ、また明日 / 明日って?
translation: Well then, see you tomorrow. / Tomorrow?

vocabulary.meaning: well then, in that case (casual transition)
quotation/echo particle (casual): '...you said?', 'what do you mean by...?'

grammar: また明日 is a standard farewell expression. 明日って? uses the quotation particle って to echo and question what was just said — 'Tomorrow? What do you mean, tomorrow?' — expressing surprise at the implication.

text: 明日は同じ船で出発でしょ? / あ、そうなの? / お話、できるよね? / うん!
translation: We're leaving on the same ship tomorrow, right? / Oh, is that so? / We can talk then, right? / Yeah!

vocabulary.meaning: right?, isn't it? (seeking confirmation, casual form of でしょう)
is that so?, really? (feminine/neutral soft surprise)
right? isn't that so? (seeking gentle confirmation)

grammar: でしょ and よね are both confirmation-seeking endings; でしょ is slightly more assertive while よね is softer. そうなの expresses mild surprise or realisation in a warm register. The rapid exchange of short lines captures natural conversational back-and-forth.

text: ザナルカンドのこと、聞かせてね!
translation: Tell me about Zanarkand!

vocabulary.meaning: to let someone hear, to tell (causative of 聞く)

grammar: 聞かせてね is a gentle imperative — the て-form + ね makes it an endearing request rather than a demand. ザナルカンドのこと uses のこと to turn the proper noun into a topic ('things about/regarding Zanarkand').

text: かわいいだろ?
translation: She's cute, right?
grammar: だろ is the casual masculine form of だろう, used here to seek agreement — Tidus nudging Wakka or Lulu to confirm that Yuna is cute. The subject is entirely dropped, understood from context.

text: 好きになるのよ / そんなの約束できないね
translation: You're going to fall for her. / I can't promise something like that.

vocabulary.meaning: to come to like, to fall for someone
something like that, that sort of thing

grammar: 好きになるのよ — Lulu predicts Tidus will develop feelings for Yuna, stated with feminine certainty using のよ. そんなの約束できない — Tidus deflects, using そんなの (that kind of thing) to dismiss the premise: he can't promise he won't like her.

text: 向こうが、俺のこと好きになったらどうするよ / そんなことにはならない
translation: What if she falls for me? / That's not going to happen.

vocabulary.meaning: that person, the other party (lit: over there)
to come to like, to fall for
what would you/we do if ~ happens?

vocabulary.word: そんなことにはならない
vocabulary.reading: そんなことにはならない
vocabulary.meaning: it won't come to that, that won't happen

grammar: 〜たらどうする is a conditional 'what if' construction: 好きになったら (if she falls for me) + どうする (what do you do). Lulu's flat response そんなことにはならない uses the になる + negative to deny the premise entirely — dry and blunt.

text: 眠くなってきたら俺に言え / 寝床の用意してやるから
translation: If you get sleepy, tell me. / I'll get your sleeping spot ready.

vocabulary.meaning: to come to ~, to start becoming (gradual change)
tell (me), say (plain imperative of 言う)
to do for someone (gruff or condescending nuance, masculine)

grammar: 眠くなってくる uses 〜てくる to indicate a gradual onset — 'if sleepiness starts coming on.' 言え is a plain imperative, casual but not harsh here. してやる (from してやる) is a masculine form of doing something for another, with a slightly rough but caring nuance — Wakka's typical register.

text: 船来ないな / 早く来ないとみんなに見つかっちゃうね
translation: The ship's not coming. / If it doesn't come soon, everyone will find us.

vocabulary.meaning: to be found, to be discovered (intransitive)
to end up doing, to go and do (contraction of 〜てしまう)

grammar: 来ないな — negative present + な expresses mild disappointment or resigned observation. 早く来ないと is a truncated conditional: 'if it doesn't come soon [something bad will happen].' 見つかっちゃう combines 見つかる (passive discovery) with ちゃう — 'we'll end up being found.'

text: 本当にいいのか
translation: Are you really sure about this?

vocabulary.meaning: is it that ~? (plain masculine question seeking confirmation or expressing doubt)

grammar: のか is a plain-register question marker that adds a slightly pressing or sceptical tone — 'is it really okay?' Dropping the subject entirely is natural; the referent (this plan, what you're doing) is obvious from context.

text: ザナルカンドに連れてって
translation: Take me to Zanarkand.

vocabulary.meaning: to take (someone somewhere), to bring along
contracted casual request form of 〜ていって (please take/go)

grammar: 連れてって is a casual contraction of 連れていって — the て-form of 連れて行く contracted further in speech. Used as a soft imperative / request: 'please take me.' The destination ザナルカンドに marks the goal with the directional particle に.

text: こらー!
translation: Hey! What are you doing!

vocabulary.meaning: hey! (reprimand, used to call out or scold someone)

grammar: こら is a spontaneous exclamation used to reprimand or get someone's attention in a scolding way. The elongated ー conveys indignation. No other words needed — the tone says everything.

text: あたしと旅するって言ったのに
translation: You said you'd travel with me!

vocabulary.meaning: to travel, to go on a journey
even though, despite (expresses disappointment or reproach)

grammar: 〜って言ったのに is a classic reproach construction: 'you said X, yet (you're not doing it).' のに here is not a purpose conjunction but a contrastive/complaint particle — expressing that the expectation was set but not met. あたし is the feminine casual first-person pronoun.

text: あれは / って言われたくせに / そっか
translation: Well, that was… / Even though you were told to! / Oh, I see.

vocabulary.meaning: even though, despite (expresses reproach or contradiction)

grammar: あれは trailing off indicates Tidus is backpedaling or making an excuse. 〜くせに is a stronger reproach than のに — it implies the speaker finds the other's behaviour inconsistent or hypocritical. そっか (contracted そうか) is a casual expression of realisation.

text: いや、あのほん / そう、だからあたしと行くの
translation: No, well, you see— / Right, that's why you're coming with me.

vocabulary.meaning: sentence-final の: assertion or explanation (feminine tone)

grammar: いや、あのほん is a flustered, incomplete attempt at an excuse — the speaker trails off (ほん → probably ほんとうは). だからあたしと行くの uses の as a firm feminine assertion: 'that's exactly why you'll go with me.' The logic is circular but delivered with confidence.

text: なーにやってんだ
translation: What the heck are you doing?

vocabulary.meaning: doing, up to (casual progressive of やる)

grammar: なーに is an elongated/emphatic なに expressing exasperation. やってんだ contracts やっているんだ — the progressive ている + explanatory んだ in colloquial speech. The whole phrase is a rhetorical reproach: 'just what do you think you're doing?'

text: ガキのくせに女と旅だ? / 千年早いって
translation: A kid like you traveling with a woman? / You've got a thousand years to go!

vocabulary.meaning: even though you're just a ~, for someone who's only a ~
a thousand years too early (idiom: you're nowhere near ready)
I'm telling you, you know (emphatic quotation marker at sentence end)

grammar: 〜のくせに expresses contempt: 'for someone who is only a kid.' 千年早い is a fixed idiom — literally 'a thousand years too early' — meaning 'you're nowhere near mature enough for this.' って at sentence end is an emphatic quotation-style ender, like 'I'm telling you!'

text: おーお、また始まるのかな?
translation: Oh boy, is it starting again?

vocabulary.meaning: oh boy, oh my (expression of amused resignation)
I wonder if ~ (soft rhetorical question, resignation or amusement)

grammar: のかな is a softened rhetorical question — the speaker isn't really asking, but musing aloud with mild exasperation. また suggests this is a recurring pattern. The overall tone is a bystander bracing for a familiar argument.

text: 泣くぞ、すぐ泣くぞ、絶対泣くぞ、ほら泣くぞ / 大っ嫌いだ
translation: You're going to cry, you'll cry right away, you'll definitely cry, see — you're going to cry! / I hate you!

vocabulary.meaning: see!, look! (drawing attention to something happening)
I hate (you/it) intensely (大 intensifies 嫌い)

grammar: Repetition of 泣くぞ escalates to provoke an emotional reaction — a teasing tactic. ほら marks the supposed moment it comes true. 大っ嫌い intensifies 嫌い with the prefix 大 (だい), and the small っ adds extra punch. だ at the end is a plain declarative of strong emotion.

text: 聞こえねぇな / もっと大きな声で言わないとダメだよ
translation: Can't hear you! / You have to say it with a louder voice!

vocabulary.meaning: a loud voice, a big voice
must do ~, have to do ~ (if you don't, it's no good)

grammar: 聞こえねぇ is a rough masculine contraction of 聞こえない — the ない→ねぇ shift is typical of gruff or provocative speech. 言わないとダメだ is a colloquial obligation pattern: 'if you don't say it, it's no good' = 'you have to say it.'

text: 大っ嫌いだ
translation: I hate you!
grammar: A repeat of the earlier outburst, now said louder as demanded. The declarative だ reinforces this as a statement of feeling rather than a question. In context, this is likely a cathartic release of pent-up emotion — shouting what she really feels.

text: ほら、頑張れ! / ほら、頑張れ!
translation: Come on, keep going! / Come on, keep going!

vocabulary.meaning: do your best!, hang in there! (plain imperative of 頑張る)

grammar: 頑張れ is the plain imperative of 頑張る — direct and energetic, used to cheer someone on. ほら here acts as an encouragement particle ('come on!'). The repetition drives emotional escalation — pressing her to keep going.

text: 大っ嫌いだ! / もう死んでしまったのよ
translation: I hate you! / He's already dead and gone.

vocabulary.meaning: already, now (indicating a state has been reached)
has died, is dead and gone (〜てしまう expressing completion with finality)

grammar: 死んでしまった uses 〜てしまう in past tense — this expresses not just death but the sense of irreversible finality. のよ is Lulu's or a female character's assertive tone, gently but firmly pointing out an unchangeable fact. This is a critical emotional moment — someone (likely Wakka's brother Chappu) is being confirmed dead.

text: だって… / だって? / でも?
translation: But… / But what? / But still?
grammar: だって trailing off is a classic pattern of someone starting to make an excuse or protest but unable to finish — implying grief, helplessness, or denial. Lulu echoes it as a pointed question ('but what?'), and then でも? shows she isn't finished — still expecting a proper reply. All three are sentence fragments.

text: 聞き飽きたわ
translation: I'm tired of hearing it.

vocabulary.meaning: to get tired of hearing, to be sick of listening to
sentence-final particle (feminine, soft assertion or resignation)

grammar: 聞き飽きる is a compound verb: 聞く (to hear) + 飽きる (to get tired of). The past tense 聞き飽きた means the state of being fed up has already been reached. わ softens the assertion slightly — Lulu's characteristic controlled, weary delivery.

text: 怖いなあ…
translation: She's scary…

vocabulary.meaning: sentence-final particle expressing feeling or reflection (masculine)

grammar: 怖いなあ is a simple exclamation of impressed fear or awe — Tidus reacting to Lulu's fierce personality. なあ (elongated な) is a masculine reflective particle, adding a lingering sense of awe or exasperation.

text: チャップって? / 俺の弟だ
translation: Chappu? / He's my little brother.

vocabulary.meaning: quotation/echo marker (asking about a name or term)

grammar: チャップって? uses って as an echo/question marker — asking 'who/what is Chappu?' A minimal, casual way to ask for clarification about a name or reference just mentioned. 俺の弟だ is a flat plain-style identification: 'He is my younger brother.' No hedging — stated simply.

text: お前に似てたんだ / 死んだ?
translation: He resembled you. / He died?

vocabulary.meaning: was doing / was (contraction of 〜ていた, past progressive)

grammar: 似てたんだ contracts 似ていたんだ: past progressive (was resembling = resembled) + んだ for personal explanation. The statement hints at why Wakka took an interest in Tidus. 死んだ? is a blunt question with no か — the rising intonation in speech makes it a question; the starkness reflects shock.

text: 討伐隊に入ってたけど / 去年シンと戦って
translation: He was in the crusaders, but / last year he fought Sin and…

vocabulary.meaning: crusaders (lit: subjugation force — the anti-Sin militia in FFX)
was doing, but… (past progressive + concessive, trailing off)

grammar: 入ってたけど contracts 入っていたけど — past progressive + けど (but). The trailing sentence sets up what comes next. 戦って is the て-form of 戦う, leaving the sentence incomplete — the listener is made to wait for the painful conclusion.

text: やられた
translation: He was killed.

vocabulary.meaning: to be defeated, to be killed, to get taken out (passive of やる)

grammar: やられた is the plain past passive of やる — informal but devastating in context. It avoids the bluntness of 死んだ while conveying the same finality. The single-word sentence, delivered after the build-up, hits hard.

text: 俺がそれを知ったのは大会の日でな
translation: The day I found out was the day of the tournament.

vocabulary.meaning: to know, to learn, to find out
nominaliser + topic marker: 'the thing that ~', 'when I ~'
and, you see (copula + na, trailing narrative)

grammar: 俺がそれを知ったのは uses nominalization — 知ったの turns the clause into a noun, then は makes it the topic: 'the thing/time that I learned about it.' 大会の日でな — でな is a soft narrative connector (like でね but more masculine), leading into the next thought.

text: それで? / 俺はガードになってシンと戦うことにした
translation: And? / So I decided to become a guardian and fight Sin.

vocabulary.meaning: and then, and so, what happened next?
guardian (FFX: one who protects a summoner)
to decide to ~, to make it a rule to ~

grammar: それで? is a prompt to continue — 'and then what?' 〜ことにした expresses a deliberate decision made at a point in the past: 'I decided to become a guardian.' The て-form chain ガードになってシンと戦う links two actions: first become a guardian, then fight Sin.

text: 仇討ちか / そのつもりだったけどな / 払っちゃうよな
translation: Revenge, huh. / That was the idea, but… / You end up just brushing it off, don't you.

vocabulary.meaning: revenge, vengeance (lit: striking down one's enemy)
that was the plan, but… (past copula + concessive + na)
to brush off, to sweep away, to wave aside
end up doing (〜てしまう contracted)

grammar: 仇討ちか — か here marks a soft rhetorical confirmation/realization ('so it was revenge'). そのつもりだったけどな — つもり expresses original intent, けどな trails off with gentle resignation. 払っちゃうよな — you end up just pushing it aside; the nuance is that grief gets suppressed by the demands of life.

text: 弟の仇討ちとブリッツ / どっちが大事だってんだよな
translation: My brother's revenge or blitzball — which one actually matters, right?

vocabulary.meaning: I'm asking which it is, you know (rhetorical: だと言っているんだ + よな)

grammar: だってんだよな is a colloquial chain: だ (copula) + って (quotation/rhetorical) + んだ (explanatory) + よ (assertion) + な (seeking agreement). The whole phrase is rhetorically self-directed — Wakka musing aloud about his own confused priorities.

text: ま、次の大会終わったらガードに専念すっから
translation: Well, once the next tournament is over, I'll focus on being a guardian.

vocabulary.meaning: once it's over, when it ends (conditional)
to devote oneself, to concentrate on
will do, because (colloquial contraction of するから)

grammar: 〜たら is a conditional 'when/if it happens' — here with clear expectation that the tournament will end. すっから contracts するから: 'because I'll do it' / 'I will, so.' The overall tone is Wakka rationalizing a compromise between his two commitments.

text: そのためにお前を利用してるみたいだけど / 悪いな
translation: It's like I'm using you for that, though. / Sorry about that.

vocabulary.meaning: for that purpose, to that end
to use, to make use of (often with slightly exploitative nuance)
sorry about that, my bad (casual apology, lit: it's bad/wrong)

grammar: 〜みたいだ is an appearance/resemblance auxiliary — Wakka frames his own exploitation self-consciously, using it to soften the admission. 悪いな is a casual masculine apology: 悪い (bad/wrong) + な (emotional particle). Literally: 'That's bad (of me)' = 'I'm sorry about it.'

text: 気にすんなよ / 俺だって、あんたに頼りっきりだ。
translation: Don't worry about it. / I'm completely relying on you too.

vocabulary.meaning: don't do ~ (colloquial negative imperative: するな contracted)
completely relying on, depending entirely on (〜っきり: nothing but)

grammar: 気にすんなよ contracts 気にするなよ — casual negative imperative. だって here means 'even I' or 'I too,' indicating Tidus is not just a recipient but equally dependent. 頼りっきり uses the っきり suffix to express total reliance: 'I'm leaning on you for everything.'

text: あんたに会えて、本当に助かってる。 / いろいろ…
translation: Meeting you has really saved me. / In so many ways…

vocabulary.meaning: being able to meet (potential て-form of 会う)
to be saved, to be helped out, to be a great help

grammar: 会えて uses the potential form (会える) in て-form — 'having been able to meet you.' 助かってる is the progressive form of 助かる: 'I continue to be saved/helped.' The trailing いろいろ… leaves the full extent unsaid — emotionally suggestive.

text: ありがとな、ワッカ。
translation: Thank you, Wakka.

vocabulary.meaning: thanks (casual masculine form of ありがとう)

grammar: ありがとな is a contracted, masculine casual form of ありがとう — the う is dropped and な (affective particle) is added. More intimate and less formal than ありがとうございます. The direct address ワッカ shows the bond that's formed.

text: 照れるからやめろ!
translation: Stop it, you're making me blush!

vocabulary.meaning: to be embarrassed, to feel shy, to blush

grammar: 照れるから uses から as a reason clause: 'because I get embarrassed.' やめろ is the plain (rough) imperative of やめる: 'stop it.' The combination — blunt command justified by embarrassment — is characteristically Wakka: too proud to accept thanks gracefully.

text: よう、ネボスケ。お前にやろうと思ってな。 / すげえ!もらっていいのか?
translation: Hey, sleepyhead. I was thinking of giving this to you. / Wow! Can I really have it?

vocabulary.meaning: to give (to someone of lower or equal status)
I was thinking (of doing), you know (と思って + な)
awesome, incredible (rough colloquial form of すごい)

grammar: やろうと思ってな — the volitional やろう (I'll give) + と思って (was thinking) + な (soft, trailing) conveys a warm, slightly hesitant intention. すげえ contracts すごい in rough speech. もらっていいのか? — もらう (to receive) + ていいのか (is it okay to?) — asking permission to accept.

text: おう!使ってくれ!
translation: Yeah! Use it!

vocabulary.meaning: please do (for me) — masculine request form

grammar: おう is a rough masculine yes. 使ってくれ is an informal request using くれ (plain imperative of くれる) — 'do the favor of using it.' More direct than 使ってください, with warmth rather than rudeness in this context.

text: それ、チャップにあげたやつ / 気にすんな!あいつは一度も使わなかった
translation: That was the one I gave to Chappu. / Don't worry about it! He never used it even once.

vocabulary.meaning: thing, one (casual, referring to an object)
not even once (emphatic negation with 一度も)

grammar: 〜やつ is a casual nominalizer for objects (like もの but rougher) — 'the one that I gave.' あいつ is a rough third-person pronoun ('that guy'). 一度も使わなかった uses 一度も with negative to mean 'not even once' — Wakka rationalizing why giving it away doesn't dishonor Chappu's memory.

text: ユーナ、遅いな / ユーナと同じ船なんだろ?先に行ってればいいんじゃないのか?
translation: Yuna's late, huh. / You're on the same ship as Yuna, right? Wouldn't it be fine for you to go ahead?

vocabulary.word: 〜てればいいんじゃないのか
vocabulary.reading: 〜てればいいんじゃないのか
vocabulary.meaning: wouldn't it be fine if you just ~ (rhetorical suggestion)

grammar: 遅いな — な adds a reflective, slightly resigned observation ('she's late, isn't she'). 先に行ってればいい contracts 先に行っていればいい — conditional progressive: 'if you go ahead, it should be fine.' じゃないのか adds a rhetorical softening: 'isn't that right?'

text: 10年前、ユーナはこの村に来た / 奈義説が始まった年だ / 奈義説?
translation: Ten years ago, Yuna came to this village. / It was the year the Eternal Calm began. / The Eternal Calm?

vocabulary.reading: なぎやすみ / なぎせつ
vocabulary.meaning: Eternal Calm (the period of peace after Sin is defeated; ナギ節 in standard script)
